text:
By Kara Adams ,
30 minutes ago
MICHIGAN (WLNS) – It was an exciting afternoon for many high school athletes and their families, as at least four athletes signed their national letter of intent on Wednesday afternoon to play collegiately at the next level.
At East Lansing, Paul VanDam signed to play baseball at Michigan State, and Drew Rensing signed to play soccer at Michigan State, under his dad and head coach, Damon Rensing.
For VanDam he knew he always wanted to stay local, and since his visit in the fall, he knew Michigan State was “where he wanted to be.”
“I’ve loved this sport my whole life, so I’ve put in the work to get to this point, and I’m excited to continue working hard and seeing what I can do in the green and white,” said VanDam.
As for the Rensings, this will be the first time that Damon Rensing has ever coached his son Drew. Drew, laughing, said his mom is “a little worried about” about the father son coaching dynamic, but nonetheless both Drew and Damon are excited to share this time with each other when Drew arrives on campus in January. Drew is graduating early from East Lansing High School and will enroll at MSU starting in January.
“We do give up a lot as coaches, and I’ve missed a lot of games, practices, car rides, doing my job, so the fact that I get to walk out to training every day and see my son whether he’s an All-American, or sits the bench, to me it’ll be special either way,” said Damon.
At Fowler High School, senior Saige Miller signed to continue her softball career and education with the University of Maryland.
Surrounded by family, friends, teammates and other members of the Fowler community, Miller says she more than excited to get to work at Maryland as she says signing to play in college is a dream come true.
“When I went on the visit I really liked the coaches,” said Miller. “Coach Lauren (Karn), coach Kate (Katey Hendershott) and coach Jen (Lapicki). Their facilities are super nice and I thought it was a great fit for me.”
For Miller, she says by signing with Maryland she also wanted to be an inspiration to other athletes at her school, that though they attend a small school, the sky is the limit on what they can achieve in life.
Former Fowler softball coach Tim Andros has been watching Miller play since she was a young child and says he couldn’t be more proud of the hard work and dedication she has put in over the years.
“It’s been really exciting to be able to coach her and to see her reach her potential, her dreams and everything like that,” said Andros. “I’ve known her since she was a little girl and she always loved softball, and you could tell there was something special about her.”
At Haslett High School, standout lacrosse player Abby Russell signed with Pitt on Wednesday.
Russell did it with her parents by her side, as well as family, teammates and coaches from Haslett in attendance.
The senior led the Vikings to the state semifinals the last three years and was a first-team All-state selection as a freshman and junior. She was also a USA lacrosse All-American this past season.
Last year, Russell committed to Pitt and will play lacrosse at the college level just like her sister did at Kent State.
“it’s so surreal,” Russell said. “I’ve literally been waiting for this moment my entire life. I remember being here seven years ago, watching my older sister sign, and ever since then, it’s just something that I knew that I wanted to do. So that’s what I worked for this entire time.”
